## A warm wedding miniature in A harmonic minor

**4/4 · Andante, ♩ = 76 · Key signature: no sharps or flats**  
Play the right hand legato at **p**, with the left hand a little softer. Start a small swell in bar 5, then ease back to **p** for the cadence. The **G♯** is the raised seventh of A harmonic minor; **F stays natural**.

**How to read it:** Each right-hand note is an eighth note; the `|` inside a bar marks beat 3. In the left hand, play the bass note on beat 1 and the two notes in parentheses **together** on beat 3, unless otherwise indicated. C4 is middle C.

| Bar | Chord | Right hand — eighth notes | Left hand |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Am** | C4 E4 G♯4 A4 \| G♯4 E4 B3 A3 | A2 → (C3 + E3) |
| 2 | **Dm/F** | D4 F4 A4 F4 \| E4 F4 E4 D4 | F2 → (A2 + D3) |
| 3 | **Am/C** | C4 E4 A4 E4 \| C4 E4 A4 C5 | C3 → (E3 + A3) |
| 4 | **E** | B4 G♯4 E4 G♯4 \| B4 A4 G♯4 E4 | E2 → (G♯2 + B2) |
| 5 | **Am** | C4 E4 G♯4 A4 \| G♯4 E4 B3 A3 | A2 → (C3 + E3) |
| 6 | **Dm/F** | D4 F4 A4 F4 \| D4 F4 E4 D4 | F2 → (A2 + D3) |
| 7 | **Am/C → E7** | C4 E4 A4 E4 \| B3 D4 E4 G♯4 | Beat 1: C3 + E3 + A3. Beat 3: E2 + B2 + D3. |
| 8 | **Am** | A4 C5 B4 A4 \| A4 A4 A4 A4 *(tie the last five A’s)* | A2 → (C3 + E3) |

The opening keeps your six-note motif recognizable, with **G♯** in place of G. For the ending, let the **G♯–A** across bars 7–8 do the work: land softly on A rather than accenting it, then let the little **C–B–A** turn settle into the held note. A slight ritardando over the last two beats is enough.

### 1. Bars 1–6: Alberti-bass option

Keep the right hand unchanged. For each left-hand voicing, play **low–high–middle–high** twice. You can leave your hand in one position for the whole bar.

| Bar | Chord | Left hand — eighth notes |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Am** | A2 E3 C3 E3 \| A2 E3 C3 E3 |
| 2 | **Dm/F** | F2 D3 A2 D3 \| F2 D3 A2 D3 |
| 3 | **Am/C** | C3 A3 E3 A3 \| C3 A3 E3 A3 |
| 4 | **E** | E2 B2 G♯2 B2 \| E2 B2 G♯2 B2 |
| 5 | **Am** | A2 E3 C3 E3 \| A2 E3 C3 E3 |
| 6 | **Dm/F** | F2 D3 A2 D3 \| F2 D3 A2 D3 |

### 2. Alternate ending: gentle plagal cadence

In A harmonic minor, the plagal cadence is **iv → i (Dm → Am)**: the D chord uses **F natural**, not F♯. Keep the same left-hand shape in bar 7, then thin it out in bar 8 so the ending settles.

| Bar | Chord | Right hand — eighth notes | Left hand — eighth notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 7 | **Dm** | A4 F4 E4 D4 \| F4 E4 D4 F4 | D3 A3 F3 A3 \| D3 A3 F3 A3 |
| 8 | **Am** | E4 C4 B3 A3 \| A3 A3 A3 A3 *(tie the last five A’s)* | A2 E3 C3 E3 \| A2 rest rest rest |

Let the **F–E** across the barline be the expressive moment. Without a G♯–A leading-tone pull in the ending, the final A feels more like a quiet arrival.
